text:
sara-support: FYI customer #1492 hitting JSON parsing failures in structured output mode. They say it worked yesterday but now our strict parser throws \"type mismatch\" on user_id and flags. Ticket attached: https://redwood.support/t/1492 :grimacing:

sara-support: Repro from their logs (root request happened at 2026-04-05T18:20:34Z). They call /v1/generate with response_mode=\"structured\" and a JSON schema. The model returned something that fails our validator.

sara-support: Request payload (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-open-7b\",
  \"response_mode\": \"structured\",
  \"json_schema\": {
    \"type\": \"object\",
    \"properties\": {
      \"user_id\": {\"type\": \"integer\"},
      \"is_premium\": {\"type\": \"boolean\"},
      \"status\": {\"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"ACTIVE\", \"INACTIVE\"]}
    },
    \"required\": [\"user_id\", \"is_premium\", \"status\"]
  }
}
```

sara-support: Model output (exact text blob they received):
```json
{
  \"user_id\": \"12345\",            // quoted number (causes integer parse fail)
  \"is_premium\": null,               // null instead of boolean
  \"status\": \"active\"              // wrong enum casing (lowercase)
}
```

sara-support: Customer saw our API respond 400 with \"JSON schema validation error: user_id must be integer\". They say their ingestion pipeline expects strict types so this blocks them from using the hosted endpoint.

tyler-ml: Thanks for the repro. Quick questions: did they pass any extra model instructions or a system prompt override? Also what content-type / accept headers did they use?

sara-support: They used standard headers: Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json. No system prompt overrides. We verified the request body exactly.

jordan-se: From the blob it looks like the model hallucinated quoting and null. Two potential mitigations: 1) At API layer, we can attempt a small, opt-in coercion pass (e.g., convert numeric strings to numbers, treat null -> false for booleans when allowed). 2) Add stricter model instructions telling the model to never emit quoted numbers or null for booleans.

jordan-se: Quick workaround for the customer: set \"strict_json\": false (if they opt-in) or run our post-processor that coerces types. I can share a short script.

sara-support: Customer asked if we can auto-coerce on their tenant. They are enterprise and will pay for a fix but need low risk.

jordan-se: Proposed patch: add a tenant-level flag \"coerce_structured_output\" default off. When enabled, the API will try simple coercions: quoted number -> number, \"null\" only allowed if schema allows nulls, try case-insensitive enum mapping. Log all coercions to audit trail.

eli-sre: FYI deploy-bot reports no runtime errors, just validator rejects. Latency for this endpoint looks normal. No infra escalations needed.

deploy-bot: deploy:validator-service v2.1.8 rolled at 2026-04-05T17:40:00Z to prod (no rollback).

sara-support: Customer wants a short-term patch or instructions to avoid. Suggested immediate steps we gave them: 1) Add explicit instruction in prompts: \"Output strictly valid JSON matching the schema: integers must be numbers, booleans true/false, enums exactly as listed (case-sensitive). Do not output null unless schema allows it.\" 2) If they control ingestion, run a small sanitize step: attempt parse then coerce numeric strings with regex, map null->false for optional flags if acceptable, and normalize enum case.

jordan-se: I'll open an RFC and a small feature ticket for tenant coercion + audit logging. Marking P2.

sara-support: Customer accepted workaround for now but asked for ETA. I promised to follow up once eng has a plan.

eli-sre: If we implement coercion please ensure it can't silently mask real schema regressions. We should emit a warning header X-Structured-Coercion: number->int and surface in logs.

sara-support: Thanks everyone — logging this thread to the ticket. Will update when RFC exists. :memo:
